lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.unitTitle: Data: Scaled Graphs and Measurement Line Plots
lessonRef.focus: a de-identified survey or measurement study
lessonRef.title: Performance task: plan: a de-identified survey or measurement study

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows how to plan before computing anything.

items.prompt: A scaled bar graph uses a scale of 5 per symbol. A bar shows 3 symbols. What does that bar represent?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Decide what the quantities are before you compute anything.

items.prompt: On a scaled bar graph with 2 per symbol, "Dogs" has 9 symbols and "Cats" has 3 symbols. How many more does "Dogs" have than "Cats"?
A line plot shows the lengths of 8 leaves, each measured to the nearest 1/4 inch: 2/4, 2/4, 4/4, 4/4, 2/4, 1/4, 3/4, 4/4. How many leaves measured exactly 4/4 inch?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Plan in writing: what you will figure out, how, and how you will check it.

items.prompt: A scaled bar graph shows a survey where each bar length equals a count of 5 per symbol. The bar for "Yellow" is worth 3 symbols. How many does "Yellow" represent?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: On a scaled bar graph with 5 per symbol, "Red" has 7 symbols and "Blue" has 3 symbols. How many more does "Red" have than "Blue"?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
